# SolveLang

> SolveLang is a readable, explainable workflow language designed for AI-assisted business processes.

SolveLang is an open-source language and workflow intelligence product. The Rust CLI is the canonical runtime for supported `.solve` workflows. Workflow Intelligence Studio provides local-first deterministic analysis. The browser preview uses a pinned WebAssembly safe-core build with host side effects denied, not the full hosted runtime.

SolveLang is not a production durable workflow engine or a general-purpose autonomous AI workforce platform.

## Working today

- Rust lexer, parser, AST runtime, interpreter, CLI, diagnostics, and hardened local execution modes
- Local-first deterministic Workflow Intelligence Studio analysis
- A pinned browser-safe core preview
- Deterministic n8n workflow preflight tools
- Public examples and documentation
- Rule-based workflow audit and support-triage planning previews; no remote tasks or messages are executed

## Deployed with gates — evidence dated September 17, 2026

- Public site hosted on AWS Amplify
- Production API access and customer-account infrastructure verified enabled
- Production API subscription billing and checkout are live
- Stripe Developer / Pro / Business prices, subscription webhook signature enforcement, and billing-failure monitoring enabled in production
- Developer, Pro, and Business API plans are purchasable today
- Paid priority and provider activation remain separate rollout gates

Deployment evidence is not a live health feed or a general-availability claim. Current health is not independently verified by the public status page.

## Experimental or test-mode

- Provider-backed AI and side-effecting HTTP, file, and environment helpers
- Provider integrations requiring scoped credentials, qualification, and explicit authorization
- Draft generation that still requires canonical validation before execution

## Planned

- Connected inbox-to-action support automation
- General managed workflow execution and broader qualified production integrations
- Additional platform evidence
- Independent uptime monitoring and operational exercises

## Important boundaries

- Workflow Intelligence Studio analysis is deterministic rather than AI analysis.
- Public audit and triage previews are rule-based, not connected autonomous agents.
- A proposed workflow or draft is not authorization for an external action.
- No production uptime, SLA, adoption, revenue, or performance benchmark is claimed.
- Private account, checkout, credentials, payment, and uploaded-workflow information is not part of the public search surface.

## Pricing facts

Prices are in US dollars and include tax: the price shown for a pack or plan is the full amount charged for it.

- Runner minutes, Standard pool (2-vCPU-class Linux machines): 5,000 minutes for $20 · 25,000 minutes for $100 · 100,000 minutes for $400.
- Runner minutes, High-Power pool (16-vCPU-class Linux machines): 1,000 minutes for $80 · 2,000 minutes for $140 · 3,000 minutes for $192 · 4,000 minutes for $236 · 5,000 minutes for $275 · 6,000 minutes for $306 · 7,000 minutes for $336 · 8,000 minutes for $360 · 9,000 minutes for $382.50 · 10,000 minutes for $400.
- Runner minutes, Premium pool (96-vCPU-class Linux machines, $0.50 per minute at every pack size): 5,000 minutes for $2,500 · 25,000 minutes for $12,500 · 100,000 minutes for $50,000.
- Runner minutes meter per second, measured from each job's own start and finish timestamps on GitHub, with a 10-second minimum per job. Most jobs run on spare Spot capacity and draw at 1×; minutes that start on guaranteed on-demand capacity draw at 2× and are always shown as a separate line. Prepaid minutes expire 12 months after purchase and never auto-renew.
- The runner-minutes pool can also be chosen per pull request with a pull request label: solvelang-runners-premium runs the pull request's jobs on the Premium pool, drawing from the Premium balance; solvelang-runners-high-power runs the pull request's jobs on the High-Power pool, drawing from the High-Power balance; solvelang-runners-standard keeps the pull request's jobs on the Standard pool, drawing from the Standard balance. The label applies per pull request; jobs already running are not moved, and a job whose workflow file already asks for a stronger pool stays on that pool.
- Faster processing is never free: it costs on-demand minutes at 2×, or work on the premium High-Power machines, which draws from the separate High-Power balance at the High-Power prices above.
- Speed Lane Cache: a 10 GB colocated cache beside the High-Power machines, $2 per month.
- API access plans, monthly: Developer $49 · Pro $199 · Business $699.
- SolveLang sells only through its own embedded payment pages on solve-lang.com — never through external checkout pages.

## Job Protection

Every runner minute includes SolveLang Job Protection: you are billed only for jobs a SolveLang machine actually ran, exactly once, metered per second from the job's own GitHub timestamps; a reconciliation pass re-checks finished jobs so engine work is never lost or double-billed; machines are never shut down from under a running job; and jobs are spread across availability zones and machine families so one cloud event cannot take down a whole set at once.

- [Job Protection](https://www.solve-lang.com/solutions/job-protection/): The guarantees behind every runner minute, each one live and proven
